title: DeFi Risks
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/0/body: Everything on Ethereum (transfers, swaps, approvals) needs **computation**, which is measured in units of **gas**: the more complex the action, the more gas. **Fee = gas used × price per unit of gas.** Gas price is measured in **gwei** (one billionth of an ETH), and it rises when the network is busy.
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/0/tip: With ETH at about $3,000, this fee comes to about $1.26.
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/1/prompt: A swap uses 150,000 gas, and the gas price is 10 gwei. How much ETH is the fee?
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/1/explanation: 150,000 × 10 = 1,500,000 gwei. Divided by one billion, that's 0.0015 ETH.
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/2/statement: If a transaction on Ethereum fails, you get its gas fee back in full.
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/2/explanation: The gas used up to the moment of failure is paid and doesn't come back, because the network did the computation. Only unused gas is refunded.
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/3/body: **Layer 2s**, like rollups, process transactions off Ethereum and record a summary on Ethereum, which is why their fees are **much lower**. Each network's fees are paid in **that network's own coin**: ETH on Ethereum and most of its Layer 2s, BNB on BNB Chain, and TRX on Tron.
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/4/prompt: You have 500 USDT on the Ethereum network in your wallet, but no ETH. Why can't you send it?
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/4/options/0: You need ETH to pay the gas fee
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/4/options/1: USDT can't be transferred on Ethereum
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/4/options/3: You have to stake the USDT first
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/4/explanation: Every transaction fee on Ethereum is paid in ETH, even when you're moving a different token. You always need a little ETH for gas.
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/5/body: To move assets between networks, you use a **bridge**. Bridges usually **lock** the asset on one side and mint an **equivalent copy** on the other. That makes them a big target for hackers, and some of the **biggest DeFi hacks** have hit bridges.
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/5/tip: Use the network's official bridge or a well-known one, and get its address from an official source.
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/7/prompt: Order these from least to most gas used (typically).
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/7/explanation: An ETH transfer is a fixed 21,000 gas. A token transfer runs one contract (usually tens of thousands of gas), a swap calls several contracts, and deploying a new contract usually takes hundreds of thousands to millions of gas.
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/8/prompt: You want to swap $50 of tokens on Ethereum, but the network is busy and the estimated fee is $15. What's the most sensible move?
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/8/options/0: Wait for gas to drop, or use a Layer 2
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/8/options/1: Swap right now, because gas doesn't matter
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/8/options/2: Set a really low gas limit to make it cheaper
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/8/options/3: Repeat the transaction several times in a row
lessons/defi-u3-l1/steps/8/explanation: $15 is 30% of the trade! And if you set the gas limit below what's actually needed, the transaction fails and you lose the gas it used too.
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/0/body: Before a DEX or protocol can move your ERC-20 tokens, you have to give it a **spending allowance** with an **approve** transaction. Many sites ask for an **unlimited allowance** by default, so you won't need to approve again next time.
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/1/prompt: Why does a DEX ask you for an approve transaction before your first swap of a token?
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/1/options/0: So it's allowed to move your tokens for the swap
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/1/options/2: To save your wallet's seed phrase
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/1/options/3: To make your gas fees free
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/1/explanation: A DEX contract can't touch your tokens without permission. An approval is exactly that permission, so watch who you give it to, and how much.
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/2/body: If a contract you gave an unlimited allowance to **gets hacked or turns out to be malicious**, it can take **all** of that token from your wallet, even months later. Phishing sites want exactly this: an **approval**, or a **signature** like **Permit** that grants a spending allowance without any gas.
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/2/tip: Revoke old allowances in the Token Approvals section of the network's block explorer, or with similar tools.
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/3/prompt: Months ago, you gave a DEX an unlimited allowance to spend your USDT. Now that DEX's contract has been hacked. What's the danger?
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/3/options/0: The hacker can move all the USDT in your wallet
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/3/options/1: Only your future swaps get a bit pricier
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/3/options/2: None, since you never gave out your seed phrase
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/3/options/3: Only the ETH in your wallet is at risk
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/3/explanation: An unlimited allowance means the contract can spend your USDT with no cap. If a hacker takes control of it, that permission comes along too. Revoke it right now.
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/4/statement: Revoking an old approval is a transaction itself, and it costs gas.
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/4/explanation: Revoking means setting the allowance to zero with a new transaction on the blockchain. It's usually cheap, but not free.
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/5/prompt: You went to claim a "free" airdrop, and your wallet shows a signature request called Permit for an unlimited amount of USDC. What do you do?
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/5/options/0: Reject it; this signature lets them spend my USDC
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/5/options/1: Sign it; there's no gas, so it's harmless
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/5/options/2: Sign it and change my wallet password later
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/5/options/3: Sign it, because airdrops are always free
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/5/explanation: A Permit signature grants a token spending allowance with no transaction and no gas. Changing your wallet app's password doesn't cancel it either. If you don't understand what you're signing, don't sign.
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/6/body: Even without phishing, the protocol itself may have a **bug**, its **oracle** (price source) could be manipulated, or its owner may hold an **admin key** to change the contract. That's why in DeFi you should **never put all your money in one protocol**, and only put in what you can afford to lose.
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/7/pairs/0/meani: Letting a contract spend your tokens
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/7/pairs/2/meani: Outside price source for a contract
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/7/pairs/3/meani: Owner's access to change the contract
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/8/prompt: Put the steps for safely swapping a new token on a DEX in order.
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/8/items/0: Connect your wallet to the DEX's official site
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/8/items/1: Choose the token and the swap amount
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/8/items/2: Approve only the amount you need
lessons/defi-u3-l2/steps/8/explanation: The approval always comes before the swap, because the DEX can't take your tokens without permission. A limited allowance that you revoke afterward cuts the risk from future hacks.
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/0/body: **Fiat-backed** (like USDT and USDC): the issuer says it holds reserves, like cash dollars or short-term bonds, for every token. **Crypto-backed** (like DAI): minted with collateral worth **more than** the token. **Algorithmic**: stability comes only from a supply-and-demand mechanism; the riskiest kind.
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/1/body: A **depeg** is when a stablecoin drifts away from its target price ($1). In March 2023, USDC briefly fell to about **$0.88** because part of its reserves got stuck at SVB bank, and it recovered a few days later. The algorithmic stablecoin **UST** fully collapsed in 2022 and became almost worthless.
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/2/prompt: By design, which kind of stablecoin is the riskiest?
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/2/options/1: Backed by dollar reserves and short-term bonds
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/2/options/2: Backed by crypto collateral worth more than itself
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/2/options/3: They all carry exactly the same risk
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/2/explanation: An algorithmic stablecoin has nothing behind it but trust and a supply mechanism. If trust breaks, it can go into a death spiral, like UST did.
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/3/prompt: This chart shows a made-up stablecoin. Tap the candle where the depeg started.
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/3/explanation: Until that candle, price was glued to $1; then it suddenly dropped to about 0.90. The candles after it slowly climbed back toward $1, a pattern like USDC's temporary depeg.
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/4/statement: Even a fiat-backed stablecoin can depeg.
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/4/explanation: USDC is a real example. A banking problem, doubts about reserves or a rush to cash out can push the price away from $1, at least for a while.
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/5/body: Stablecoins are **not risk-free**: there's issuer and reserve risk, contract risk and **freeze** risk, since centralized issuers can block the tokens at an address. Many people spread large balances across **several stablecoins** and are wary of very high yields on stablecoins.
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/6/prompt: You hold 10,000 units of a stablecoin, and it has depegged to $0.92. If you sell right now, how much have you lost?
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/6/explanation: 10,000 × 0.92 = $9,200, which is $800 (8%) less than $10,000. If you wait, it may recover, but there's no guarantee.
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/7/pairs/0/meani: Dollar and bond reserves held by the issuer
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/7/pairs/1/meani: Collateral worth more than the token
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/7/pairs/2/meani: Stability only from supply and demand
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/8/prompt: You keep your savings in stablecoins, and a site offers 40% APY on a new algorithmic stablecoin. Which plan makes the most sense?
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/8/options/0: Spread it across several trusted stablecoins and avoid unusual yields
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/8/options/1: Move the full $20,000 into that algorithmic stablecoin
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/8/options/2: Convert it all to a memecoin for bigger gains
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/8/options/3: Keep the whole amount on an unknown exchange
lessons/defi-u3-l3/steps/8/explanation: Sky-high yield on a brand-new algorithmic stablecoin is the same combo people saw right before UST collapsed. Diversifying and steering clear of unusual promises spreads your risk.
